text: Even after writing eleven books and winning several prestigious awards, Maya Angelou couldn’t escape the nagging
ipa: /ˈivɪn ˈæftɚ ɹˈaɪtɪŋ ɪlˈɛvən bˈʊks ənd wˈɪnɪŋ sˈɛvɹəl pɹɛstˈɪdʒəs əwˈɔɹdz mˈaɪə ˈændʒəlˌu couldnt ɪskˈeɪp ðə nˈæɡɪŋ/

text: doubt that she hadn’t really earned her accomplishments.
ipa: /dˈaʊt ðˈæt ʃˈi hadnt ɹˈɪli ˈɝnd hˈɝ əkˈɑmplɪʃmənts/

text: Albert Einstein experienced something similar: he described himself
ipa: /ˈælbɚt ˈaɪnstaɪn ɪkspˈɪɹiənst sˈʌmθɪŋ sˈɪməlɚ hˈi dɪskɹˈaɪbd hɪmsˈɛlf/

text: as an “involuntary swindler” whose work didn’t deserve as much attention as it had received.
ipa: /ˈæz ˈæn ˌɪnvˈɑləntˌɛɹi swˈɪndəlɚ hˈuz wˈɝk didnt dɪzˈɝv ˈæz mˈʌtʃ ətˈɛnʃən ˈæz ˈɪt hˈæd ɹəsˈivd/

text: Accomplishments at the level of Angelou’s or Einstein’s are rare,
ipa: /əkˈɑmplɪʃmənts ˈæt ðə lˈɛvəl ˈʌv angelous ˈɔɹ einsteins ˈɑɹ ɹˈɛɹ/

text: but their feeling of fraudulence is extremely common.
ipa: /bˈʌt ðˈɛɹ fˈilɪŋ ˈʌv fraudulence ˈɪz ɛkstɹˈimli kˈɑmən/

text: Why can’t so many of us shake feelings
ipa: /wˈaɪ kˈænt sˈoʊ mˈɛni ˈʌv ˈʌs ʃˈeɪk fˈilɪŋz/

text: that we haven’t earned our accomplishments, or that our ideas
ipa: /ðˈæt wˈi havent ˈɝnd ˈaʊɚ əkˈɑmplɪʃmənts ˈɔɹ ðˈæt ˈaʊɚ aɪdˈiəz/

ipa: /ənd skˈɪlz ˈɑɹənt wˈɝði ˈʌv ˈʌðɚz ətˈɛnʃən/

text: Psychologist Pauline Rose Clance was the first to study this unwarranted sense of insecurity.
ipa: /saɪkˈɑlədʒəst pɔlˈin ɹˈoʊz clance wˈɑz ðə fˈɝst tˈu stˈʌdi ðˈɪs ənwˈɔɹəntɪd sˈɛns ˈʌv ˌɪnsɪkjˈʊɹɪti/

ipa: /ɪn hˈɝ wˈɝk ˈæz ə θˈɛɹəpəst ʃˈi nˈoʊtəst mˈɛni ˈʌv hˈɝ ˌʌndɚɡɹˈædʒəwət pˈeɪʃənts ʃˈɛɹd ə kənsˈɝn/

text: though they had high grades, they didn’t believe they deserved their spots at the university.
ipa: /ðˈoʊ ðˈeɪ hˈæd hˈaɪ ɡɹˈeɪdz ðˈeɪ didnt bɪlˈiv ðˈeɪ dɪzˈɝvd ðˈɛɹ spˈɑts ˈæt ðə jˌunəvˈɝsəti/

text: Some even believed their acceptance had been an admissions error.
ipa: /sˈʌm ˈivɪn bɪlˈivd ðˈɛɹ æksˈɛptəns hˈæd bˈɪn ˈæn ædmˈɪʃənz ˈɛɹɚ/

text: While Clance knew these fears were unfounded, she could also remember feeling the exact same
ipa: /wˈaɪl clance nˈu ðˈiz fˈɪɹz wˈɝ ənfˈaʊndɪd ʃˈi kˈʊd ˈɔlsoʊ ɹɪmˈɛmbɚ fˈilɪŋ ðə ɪɡzˈækt sˈeɪm/

text: way in graduate school.
ipa: /wˈeɪ ɪn ɡɹˈædʒəwət skˈul/

text: She and her patients experienced something that goes by a number of names-- imposter phenomenon, imposter
ipa: /ʃˈi ənd hˈɝ pˈeɪʃənts ɪkspˈɪɹiənst sˈʌmθɪŋ ðˈæt ɡˈoʊz bˈaɪ ə nˈʌmbɚ ˈʌv nˈeɪmz ˌɪmpˈɔstɚ fənˈɑmənˌɑn ˌɪmpˈɔstɚ/

text: experience, and imposter syndrome.
ipa: /ɪkspˈɪɹiəns ənd ˌɪmpˈɔstɚ sˈɪndɹˌoʊm/

text: Together with colleague Suzanne Imes, Clance first studied imposterism in female college students and faculty.
ipa: /təɡˈɛðɚ wˈɪð kˈɑliɡ suzˈæn ˈaɪmz clance fˈɝst stˈʌdid imposterism ɪn fˈimˌeɪl kˈɑlɪdʒ stˈudənts ənd fˈækəlti/

text: Their work established pervasive feelings of fraudulence in this group.
ipa: /ðˈɛɹ wˈɝk ɪstˈæblɪʃt pɚvˈeɪsɪv fˈilɪŋz ˈʌv fraudulence ɪn ðˈɪs ɡɹˈup/

text: Since that first study, the same thing has been established across gender, race, age,
ipa: /sˈɪns ðˈæt fˈɝst stˈʌdi ðə sˈeɪm θˈɪŋ hˈæz bˈɪn ɪstˈæblɪʃt əkɹˈɔs dʒˈɛndɚ ɹˈeɪs ˈeɪdʒ/

text: and a huge range of occupations, though it may be more prevalent
ipa: /ənd ə hjˈudʒ ɹˈeɪndʒ ˈʌv ˌɑkjəpˈeɪʃənz ðˈoʊ ˈɪt mˈeɪ bˈi mˈɔɹ pɹˈɛvələnt/

text: and disproportionately affect the experiences of underrepresented or disadvantaged groups.
ipa: /ənd dˌɪspɹəpˈɔɹʃənətli əfˈɛkt ðə ɪkspˈɪɹiənsɪz ˈʌv əndɚɹˌɛpɹɪzˈɛntɪd ˈɔɹ dɪsədvˈæntɪdʒd ɡɹˈups/

text: To call it a syndrome is to downplay how universal
ipa: /tˈu kˈɔl ˈɪt ə sˈɪndɹˌoʊm ˈɪz tˈu dˈaʊnplˌeɪ hˈaʊ jˌunəvˈɝsəl/

text: it is. It's not a disease or an abnormality, and it isn’t necessarily tied
ipa: /ˈɪt ˈɪz ˈɪts nˈɑt ə dɪzˈiz ˈɔɹ ˈæn ˌæbnɔɹmˈæləti ənd ˈɪt isnt nˌɛsəsˈɛɹəli tˈaɪd/

text: to depression, anxiety, or self-esteem.
ipa: /tˈu dɪpɹˈɛʃən æŋzˈaɪəti ˈɔɹ selfesteem/

text: Where do these feelings of fraudulence come from? People who are highly
ipa: /wˈɛɹ dˈu ðˈiz fˈilɪŋz ˈʌv fraudulence kˈʌm fɹˈʌm pˈipəl hˈu ˈɑɹ hˈaɪli/

text: skilled or accomplished tend to think others are just as skilled.
ipa: /skˈɪld ˈɔɹ əkˈɑmplɪʃt tˈɛnd tˈu θˈɪŋk ˈʌðɚz ˈɑɹ dʒˈʌst ˈæz skˈɪld/

text: This can spiral into feelings that they don’t deserve accolades and opportunities over other people.
ipa: /ðˈɪs kˈæn spˈaɪɹəl ˈɪntu fˈilɪŋz ðˈæt ðˈeɪ dont dɪzˈɝv ˈækəlˌeɪdz ənd ˌɑpɚtˈunətiz ˈoʊvɚ ˈʌðɚ pˈipəl/

text: And as Angelou and Einstein experienced, there’s often no threshold of accomplishment
ipa: /ənd ˈæz ˈændʒəlˌu ənd ˈaɪnstaɪn ɪkspˈɪɹiənst theres ˈɔfən nˈoʊ θɹˈɛʃˌoʊld ˈʌv əkˈɑmplɪʃmənt/

text: that puts these feelings to rest.
ipa: /ðˈæt pˈʊts ðˈiz fˈilɪŋz tˈu ɹˈɛst/

text: Feelings of imposterism aren’t restricted to highly skilled individuals, either.
ipa: /fˈilɪŋz ˈʌv imposterism ˈɑɹənt ɹistɹˈɪktəd tˈu hˈaɪli skˈɪld ˌɪndəvˈɪdʒəwəlz ˈiðɚ/

text: Everyone is susceptible to a phenomenon known as pluralistic ignorance,
ipa: /ˈɛvɹiwˌʌn ˈɪz səsˈɛptəbəl tˈu ə fənˈɑmənˌɑn nˈoʊn ˈæz plˌʊɹəlˈɪstɪk ˈɪɡnɚəns/

text: where we each doubt ourselves privately, but believe we’re alone in thinking
ipa: /wˈɛɹ wˈi ˈitʃ dˈaʊt aʊɚsˈɛlvz pɹˈaɪvətli bˈʌt bɪlˈiv wˈɝ əlˈoʊn ɪn θˈɪŋkɪŋ/

text: that way because no one else voices their doubts.
ipa: /ðˈæt wˈeɪ bɪkˈɔz nˈoʊ wˈʌn ˈɛls vˈɔɪsəz ðˈɛɹ dˈaʊts/

text: Since it’s tough to really know how hard our peers work,
ipa: /sˈɪns ˈɪts tˈʌf tˈu ɹˈɪli nˈoʊ hˈaʊ hˈɑɹd ˈaʊɚ pˈɪɹz wˈɝk/

text: how difficult they find certain tasks.
ipa: /hˈaʊ dˈɪfəkəlt ðˈeɪ fˈaɪnd sˈɝtən tˈæsks/

text: Or how much they doubt themselves, there’s no easy way to dismiss feelings
ipa: /ˈɔɹ hˈaʊ mˈʌtʃ ðˈeɪ dˈaʊt ðɛmsˈɛlvz theres nˈoʊ ˈizi wˈeɪ tˈu dɪsmˈɪs fˈilɪŋz/

text: that we’re less capable than the people around us.
ipa: /ðˈæt wˈɝ lˈɛs kˈeɪpəbəl ðˈæn ðə pˈipəl ɚˈaʊnd ˈʌs/

text: Intense feelings of imposterism can prevent people from sharing their great ideas
ipa: /ˌɪntˈɛns fˈilɪŋz ˈʌv imposterism kˈæn pɹɪvˈɛnt pˈipəl fɹˈʌm ʃˈɛɹɪŋ ðˈɛɹ ɡɹˈeɪt aɪdˈiəz/

text: or applying for jobs and programs where they’d excel.
ipa: /ˈɔɹ əplˈaɪɪŋ fˈɔɹ dʒˈɑbz ənd pɹˈoʊɡɹˌæmz wˈɛɹ theyd ɪksˈɛl/

text: At least so far, the most surefire way to combat imposter syndrome
ipa: /ˈæt lˈist sˈoʊ fˈɑɹ ðə mˈoʊst surefire wˈeɪ tˈu kˈɑmbæt ˌɪmpˈɔstɚ sˈɪndɹˌoʊm/

text: is to talk about it. Many people suffering from imposter syndrome are afraid
ipa: /ˈɪz tˈu tˈɔk əbˈaʊt ˈɪt mˈɛni pˈipəl sˈʌfɚɪŋ fɹˈʌm ˌɪmpˈɔstɚ sˈɪndɹˌoʊm ˈɑɹ əfɹˈeɪd/

text: that if they ask about their performance, their fears will be confirmed.
ipa: /ðˈæt ˈɪf ðˈeɪ ˈæsk əbˈaʊt ðˈɛɹ pɚfˈɔɹməns ðˈɛɹ fˈɪɹz wˈɪl bˈi kənfˈɝmd/

text: And even when they receive positive feedback, it often fails to ease feelings of fraudulence.
ipa: /ənd ˈivɪn wˈɛn ðˈeɪ ɹəsˈiv pˈɑzətɪv fˈidbˌæk ˈɪt ˈɔfən fˈeɪlz tˈu ˈiz fˈilɪŋz ˈʌv fraudulence/

text: But on the other hand, hearing that an advisor
ipa: /bˈʌt ˈɑn ðə ˈʌðɚ hˈænd hˈiɹɪŋ ðˈæt ˈæn ædvˈaɪzɚ/

text: or mentor has experienced feelings of imposterism can help relieve those feelings.
ipa: /ˈɔɹ mˈɛntˌɔɹ hˈæz ɪkspˈɪɹiənst fˈilɪŋz ˈʌv imposterism kˈæn hˈɛlp ɹɪlˈiv ðˈoʊz fˈilɪŋz/

text: The same goes for peers.
ipa: /ðə sˈeɪm ɡˈoʊz fˈɔɹ pˈɪɹz/

text: Even simply finding out there’s a term for these feelings can be an incredible relief.
ipa: /ˈivɪn sˈɪmpli fˈaɪndɪŋ ˈaʊt theres ə tˈɝm fˈɔ�� ðˈiz fˈilɪŋz kˈæn bˈi ˈæn ˌɪnkɹˈɛdəbəl ɹɪlˈif/

text: Once you’re aware of the phenomenon, you can combat your own imposter syndrome by collecting
ipa: /wˈʌns youre əwˈɛɹ ˈʌv ðə fənˈɑmənˌɑn jˈu kˈæn kˈɑmbæt jˈɔɹ ˈoʊn ˌɪmpˈɔstɚ sˈɪndɹˌoʊm bˈaɪ kəlˈɛktɪŋ/

text: and revisiting positive feedback.
ipa: /ənd ɹivˈɪzɪtɪŋ pˈɑzətɪv fˈidbˌæk/

text: One scientist who kept blaming herself for problems in her lab started to document the causes
ipa: /wˈʌn sˈaɪəntɪst hˈu kˈɛpt blˈeɪmɪŋ hɚsˈɛlf fˈɔɹ pɹˈɑbləmz ɪn hˈɝ lˈæb stˈɑɹtɪd tˈu dˈɑkjəmɛnt ðə kˈɑzəz/

text: every time something went wrong.
ipa: /ˈɛvɚi tˈaɪm sˈʌmθɪŋ wˈɛnt ɹˈɔŋ/

text: Eventually, she realized most of the problems came from equipment failure,
ipa: /ɪvˈɛntʃəwəli ʃˈi ɹˈiəlˌaɪzd mˈoʊst ˈʌv ðə pɹˈɑbləmz kˈeɪm fɹˈʌm ɪkwˈɪpmənt fˈeɪljɚ/

text: and came to recognize her own competence.
ipa: /ənd kˈeɪm tˈu ɹˈɛkəɡnˌaɪz hˈɝ ˈoʊn kˈɑmpətɪns/

text: We may never be able to banish these feelings entirely,
ipa: /wˈi mˈeɪ nˈɛvɚ bˈi ˈeɪbəl tˈu bˈænɪʃ ðˈiz fˈilɪŋz ɪntˈaɪɚli/

text: but we can have open conversations about academic or professional challenges.
ipa: /bˈʌt wˈi kˈæn hˈæv ˈoʊpən kˌɑnvɚsˈeɪʃənz əbˈaʊt ˌækədˈɛmɪk ˈɔɹ pɹəfˈɛʃənəl tʃˈæləndʒɪz/

text: With increasing awareness of how common these experiences are, perhaps we can feel freer
ipa: /wˈɪð ˌɪnkɹˈisɪŋ əwˈɛɹnəs ˈʌv hˈaʊ kˈɑmən ðˈiz ɪkspˈɪɹiənsɪz ˈɑɹ pɚhˈæps wˈi kˈæn fˈil fɹˈiɚ/

text: to be frank about our feelings and build confidence in some simple truths: you have talent,
ipa: /tˈu bˈi fɹˈæŋk əbˈaʊt ˈaʊɚ fˈilɪŋz ənd bˈɪld kˈɑnfədəns ɪn sˈʌm sˈɪmpəl tɹˈuθs jˈu hˈæv tˈælənt/

text: you are capable, and you belong.
